chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: What became of the measured-music recordings; Nat's early singing
summary: Lee does not know where the measured-music tracks went and says the group sang in unison; Nat later coached girl singers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And ask you about the time that you recorded for measured music with Nat, was that ever on a record or was that anything that anybody could hear now, or did it ...
Oh, I don't think so. No -- I don't think so.
You don't know what happened to that material?

No, I have no idea -- because that didn't -- I think that lasted like a couple of years, you know, where it was, as I said, it was in the drug stores, at the fountains, or in restaurants, you know, and it was called 'measured music' you know. You could put ...
And you sang, and Nat wasn't doing any singing then, is that right?
No, we were singing with a group, like, you know? All 4 were singing.
And so he always -- a lot of unison things, you know. A lot of unison things.
But I wasn't with him when he started singing. See, I think one of the reasons that Nat could sing so well -- Nat used to do a lot of coaching of girl singers.
Oh, I can't remember these girls names who were around town; they were pretty good singers, but that's what he used to do. And when I had the band at the Club Alabam, Nat was one of the arrangers.
